hero.title: Clear aligners
hero.lead: Clear aligner treatment uses a series of clear, removable trays. Each set moves your teeth a little, until they reach their planned position.

intro.heading: How clear aligner treatment works
intro.html:
After an assessment, your dentist takes scans or impressions and plans the movement of your teeth. A series of custom aligners is made, and you change to the next set as directed. You’ll have regular reviews to check progress.

Aligners only work while they’re in your mouth. They need to be worn for most of the day and night, taken out only to eat, drink anything other than water, and clean your teeth.

items.title: Discreet
items.text: The trays are clear, so most people won’t notice them.

items.title: Removable
items.text: Take them out to eat, brush and floss.

items.title: No metal
items.text: No brackets or wires to rub your cheeks and gums.

process.heading: What to know before you start
steps: A trained dentist checks whether aligners can achieve what you need. Some people are better suited to braces or an orthodontist, and we’ll tell you if that’s the case.
X-rays, photos and moulds of your teeth are taken, and you usually start in your trays within a few weeks.
Some minor cases take as little as 7 weeks, but around 12 to 18 months is typical. Your plan will give you an estimate.
Teeth tend to drift back, so you’ll need a retainer to hold the result.

weigh.heading: Benefits and things to consider
benefits: No brackets or wires to irritate the mouth
Easier to brush and floss than with fixed braces
consider: Results depend on wearing the aligners as directed
Not suitable for every type of tooth movement
You’ll need a retainer afterwards, possibly long term

care.heading: Looking after your aligners
items: Rinse and gently clean your aligners when you take them out, and brush your teeth before putting them back in.
Take aligners out to eat and for drinks other than water.
Keep them in their case when they’re out, so they aren’t lost or damaged.

faqs: Am I suitable for clear aligners?
Only an assessment can tell. Some people are better suited to fixed braces or an orthodontist, and your dentist will be upfront about it.
Many people feel pressure or tightness for a day or two after changing to a new set. This usually settles.
How long will I need a retainer?
Teeth tend to drift back after treatment. Your dentist will recommend a retainer plan to hold the result.
cost: The cost depends on what your mouth needs, so it can only be worked out after an examination.
